summary: Independent projects that show I develop as well as test: a live full stack application, REST APIs, and cloud back ends, each with the automation and CI/CD around it. Code at github.com/shane24sweeney.
highlights: selenium-automation.com (github.com/shane24sweeney/aboutshane): designed, built, and operate a live full stack application, a React 18 + TypeScript front end and a Java 25 / Spring Boot 3.5 API on AWS, defined in CloudFormation/SAM and released only through gated CI/CD.

Back end (Java/Spring Boot): content, contact, search, status, visitor-stats, and résumé-PDF REST APIs with layered design; business logic depends on repository and notifier interfaces with DynamoDB and SES adapters supplied by constructor injection; Bean Validation returns field-level 400 errors; messages are saved before email so a mail failure never loses data; writes the site doesn't need (PUT, PATCH, DELETE) are refused with 405.

New API feature: added GET /api/content/running/stats, which parses race distances and finish times to compute totals and the personal best at each distance, and built the React section that displays them and degrades gracefully if the API is unavailable.

Front end (React/TypeScript): single-page application with React Router, typed API clients with request timeouts and cancellation, shape validation that falls back to bundled content, site search, accessible carousels, a phone layout with a bottom tab bar, pre-rendered HTML for search engines and clients without JavaScript, and interactive 3D (three.js) quality and visitor dashboards.

Cloud and DevSecOps: Lambda with SnapStart behind an HTTP API, DynamoDB, SES, private S3 behind CloudFront with origin access control, a Content Security Policy and security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame options), Route 53, 5-minute edge caching, and a 2 requests/second API throttle; pull requests with required checks on a protected branch, CodeQL, Dependabot, secret scanning, cfn-lint, ESLint, and TypeScript strict mode.

Automated testing: 176 JUnit/MockMvc backend tests, 118 Vitest unit tests, and 179 Playwright end-to-end tests on 14 browser and device configurations (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Android and iPhone phones, iPad and Android tablets; 2,400+ runs per pull request), plus 130 live production checks, API contract tests, a Postman/Newman collection, JMeter load tests, and axe accessibility and security tests.

Quality results: the latest daily run made 3,115 checks with 99.9% passing; 99% of the code is covered (UI unit and browser tests together, and the API), with minimums enforced in CI; typical response under load is 80 ms; a daily quality report is emailed and published, and shown live on the site's Quality dashboard.

E-Commerce REST API (github.com/shane24sweeney/sb-ecom): Spring Boot 3 / Java 17 service with a controller–service–repository architecture, Spring Data JPA on a relational database, DTOs mapped via ModelMapper, paginated endpoints, Bean Validation, and a global exception handler; found and fixed a defect returning 500 instead of 400, with MockMvc tests in GitHub Actions CI.
Customer CRUD API (github.com/shane24sweeney/app-crud): Spring Boot 3 REST API for customer records with constructor injection, Spring Data JPA, and H2, covered by MockMvc CRUD and 404 tests in CI.
Greeting API (github.com/shane24sweeney/apishane): Spring Boot 3.5 / Java 17 API with a CORS-restricted JSON endpoint, a bundled React page, MockMvc tests, and CI.

Playwright for .NET (C#) (github.com/shane24sweeney/PlaywrightTests): NUnit end-to-end suite on .NET 10 with Page Objects, parallel runs, tracing, and cross-browser runs on Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

More frameworks: an Appium + Java framework running Android and iOS devices in parallel locally or on BrowserStack, and Playwright + TypeScript with Cucumber and BrowserStack (automationPlaywrightTS); Claude Code is my AI pair programmer, with every change reviewed.
